answers.explanation: It's free and global, but slow to react.
It picks a backend when a connection opens and forwards all of that connection's packets to it.
One connection can carry a huge share of traffic and pin it to one backend.
It terminates HTTP and can route by host, path, method, headers, or cookies.
Otherwise every request would appear to come from the balancer.
That's part of why L4 balancers handle millions of packets per second.
No extra hop, but every client needs the logic and a current server list.
Only idempotent requests are safe to retry blindly.
